title: JavaScript Modules Applied Check
description: Test your ability to diagnose module import/export mistakes, reason about module behavior, and choose the right module pattern.
author: DailyCoder

questions.explanation: `add` is a named export, so it must be imported with curly braces unless re-exported differently.
Default exports are imported without curly braces.

questions.prompt:
What is wrong with this browser import for a local file in the same folder?
```js
import { add } from "math.js";
```

options.text: Local imports usually need `./`, so it should be `"./math.js"`
Named imports cannot use local files

questions.explanation: In browser modules, local relative imports usually start with `./` or `../`.

questions.prompt:
What does this import do?
```js
import "./setup.js";
```

options.text: Imports all exports as an object named `setup`
Runs `setup.js` for its side effects without importing names
Loads `setup.js` only after a button click

questions.explanation: A bare import like this is a side-effect import.

options.text: `import()` returns a Promise, so `math.add` is not available yet
Dynamic import cannot load local files
Dynamic import must use curly braces

questions.explanation: Dynamic `import()` is asynchronous. Use `await import(...)` or `.then(...)`.

questions.prompt: Which code correctly uses a named export from a dynamic import?
questions.explanation: Dynamic import resolves to a module object, so you can destructure named exports from it.

questions.prompt: How can a default export from `Button.js` be re-exported as a named export?
questions.explanation: The syntax `export { default as Button } from "./Button.js"` re-exports a default export under a named export.

questions.prompt: What is a likely problem with a giant `utils.js` file containing unrelated helpers?

options.text: It prevents JavaScript from using functions
It automatically turns all imports into defaults
It cannot be imported by any module

questions.explanation: A giant utility file often becomes a dumping ground. Focused module names make code easier to navigate.

options.text: A module importing itself through a loop of imports
A function with a loop inside it
A file that has no exports

questions.explanation: A circular dependency occurs when modules depend on each other directly or indirectly, such as `a.js` importing `b.js` while `b.js` imports `a.js`.

questions.prompt: What is one good way to fix two modules that import each other for shared logic?

options.text: Extract the shared logic into a third module
Convert all named exports into default exports
Remove all imports and use global variables

questions.explanation: Shared logic can often move into a separate module that both original modules import.

questions.prompt: What is true about top-level variables in ES modules?

options.text: They are scoped to the module unless exported
They can only be declared with `var`
They are deleted after each import

questions.explanation: Modules have their own scope. Top-level variables are not automatically global.

questions.prompt: What happens when a module is imported by multiple files?

options.text: The module is generally evaluated once and shared
The module is copied into a new global variable every time
The browser deletes the previous import
Imports stop working after the first file

questions.explanation: Modules are evaluated once, and later imports use the same module instance.

questions.prompt: Which import combines a default import with named imports?
questions.explanation: The default import comes first, followed by named imports in curly braces.

questions.prompt: Why might a side-effect import be harder to understand than an explicit setup function?

options.text: It hides what action is performed unless you inspect the imported file
It always imports a wrong default export

questions.explanation: A side-effect import like `import "./setup.js"` does not show the performed action at the call site.

questions.prompt: When is dynamic import usually a good choice?

options.text: For every dependency, even simple required ones
For optional or heavy code that should load only when needed

questions.explanation: Dynamic imports are useful for delayed loading, such as optional features or large modules.
